title: Four-Round Feistel Sufficiency for Reset-Secure Sources
summary: For reset-secure sources, five rounds achieve the relevant transformation; four rounds are necessary for PRP security, but whether four suffice remains open.

formal_statement.body: For reset-secure sources, determine whether a four-round Feistel construction achieves CP-sequential indifferentiability and consequently the corresponding psPRP security. Four rounds are necessary to reach PRP security, but whether four rounds are sufficient for this transformation remains unresolved.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptography concerning Feistel constructions and pseudorandom permutation security.
parameters: number of Feistel rounds, with four as the target construction depth
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a four-round Feistel construction for reset-secure sources achieves CP-sequential indifferentiability and consequently the corresponding psPRP security.

progress.summary: The source presents five-round Feistel as achieving CP-sequential indifferentiability for reset-secure sources and notes that four rounds are necessary for PRP security. It explicitly leaves the sufficiency of four rounds as an open problem.
citation_labels: Pratik Soni et al., Public-Seed Pseudorandom Permutations
